data.narrative:
Helion is a Series F-stage climate and energy technology company founded by David Kirtley and Chris Pihl, currently valued at $15.5B post-money and having raised over $1B to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies in the Climate & Energy sector: 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. This method applies a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F advancement to Helion's last known post-money valuation of $5.4B, yielding an implied valuation of $7.0B. A Peer-Median approach is not viable; while 8 same-sector peers exist, none of the narrower filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier) produced the minimum required dataset of 3 or more comparable transactions to establish reliable benchmarks. Constructing a median from the full sector peer set would introduce material noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6.0B to $8.1B, centered on $7.0B. This range reflects the median implied by stage progression alone, with bounds derived from typical variance around that method. The primary uncertainty is the absence of tight-peer transaction multiples; any valuation substantially above this range would require either material progress on operating milestones post-last-raise or a fundamental reassessment of the peer set methodology.
